title: One Tenant Fills the Queue
description: A tenant submits 50,000 two-hour transcodes ahead of other tenants' two-second thumbnails. Database capacity is bounded. How should the worker design improve fairness?

options.text: Increase the visibility timeout and keep one FIFO queue.
options.explanation: Visibility controls redelivery, not fairness between tenants or very different job sizes.

options.text: Scale workers without a ceiling until the queue is empty.
options.explanation: Unbounded workers can exhaust the downstream database and do not provide a fair scheduling policy.

options.text: Separate workload classes and enforce per-tenant concurrency with bounded worker pools.
options.explanation: Class isolation prevents long jobs from blocking short ones; tenant limits prevent monopolization while the pool ceiling protects dependencies.

options.text: Ask thumbnail clients to poll status more frequently.
options.explanation: Polling adds read load without changing when their work can start.
